answer: A Hardware security key bound by callback verification with annual re-verification ties the identity to something the applicant actually controls: the hardware security key answers a fresh challenge, the callback verification is recorded, and annual re-verification keeps one channel from spawning many identities, so a Sybil farm would need a separate real channel for every fake account. A mesa that appears twice is the tell: the same channel cannot back two identities. When the sparrow settles over the wander, the binding holds because every channel answered its own challenge.
